contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: payload overwrite replaces the whole payload of the targeted points instead of merging
contract_grounding.note: constraint_id recovered from the script header (debate_logs/state_payload_overwrite_006.py line 6) and the log DEFECT line — the candidates.jsonl constraint_id field was empty. assertion_text_quoted is the verbatim description field of the contract (structured_contract.json behavioral_contracts[].contract_id == qdrant_bc_payload_overwrite_replace_001); the contract's full entry additionally pins scenario 'set payload keys {a,b} -> PUT payload+overwrite with {c} (wait=true) -> GET the points with payload' and expected_behavior 'after overwrite the record payload equals exactly {c}; the previously stored keys {a,b} are removed (set semantics, not merge)'. Violates-declaration self-check: the DEFECT observation (B-step POST payload+set merged with the pre-existing 'orig' key) lies OUTSIDE the quoted assertion's constraint domain — the quote pins replace semantics only for the PUT payload+overwrite face and only AFTER the overwrite step; it asserts nothing about the post-set readback. The tested phenomenon is thus under the wrong constraint citation: the script's B-step EXACT-after-set expectation is grounded neither in this contract nor in the documentation. The contract's own pinned assertion was actually satisfied by the API (D readback exactly {'c': 'three'} on both points, a/b/orig removed), so api_violates_assertion=false is the genuinely-compliant branch, not vague acceptance.

log: DEFECT lines derive solely from the B-step extra oracle (2 lines, points 1 and 2); the contract's actual pinned assertion (D readback exactly {'c':'three'} with a/b absent) PASSED in the same log; the DEFECT_FOUND verdict is produced by the script's precondition oracle, not by the pinned contract
chain_trace.break_detail: Script oracle overreach (milvus_030-pattern: chain internally consistent but the defecting assertion is not the contract's assertion). The B-step 'EXACT after set' expectation is the script author's own construction: the contract's expected_behavior pins exact-equality only after the PUT overwrite, and both the official documentation ('set payload ... keeping others unchanged') and the source (PayloadStorage::set -> point_payload.merge) define POST set as key-merge. The script even planted a pre-existing {'orig':true} payload in step A and then required set to erase it — which the script's own E-step (merge expected, observed, and marked OK) contradicts. Verdict DEFECT_FOUND is a testing artifact at the script link; contract, doc, and the API's actual behavior are mutually consistent.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST set face: REST #[post] set_payload (update_api.rs:194) -> do_set_payload -> PayloadOps::SetPayload (src/common/update.rs:600) -> process_payload_operation (lib/shard/src/update.rs:106) -> segment set_payload (entry.rs:751) -> struct_payload_index set_payload (:934) -> payload storage set (in_memory_payload_storage_impl.rs:77) -> point_payload.merge(payload) = MERGE. PUT overwrite face: REST #[put] overwrite_payload (update_api.rs:227) -> do_overwrite_payload -> PayloadOps::OverwritePayload (src/common/update.rs:647) -> process_payload_operation (lib/shard/src/update.rs:137) -> segment set_full_payload (entry.rs:737) -> struct_payload_index overwrite_payload (:909) -> payload storage overwrite (in_memory_payload_storage_impl.rs:67) -> payload.insert(...) = FULL REPLACE. The two faces are deliberately distinct primitives end to end; no validation is missing — the distinction IS the feature.
source_grounding.note: by_design evidence is explicit at three layers: (1) enum doc comments 'Set payload value, overrides if it is already exists' vs 'Overwrite full payload with given keys' (lib/shard/src/operations/payload_ops.rs:17,25); (2) dedicated storage primitives with a literal merge call vs insert call (in_memory_payload_storage_impl.rs:77-90); (3) maintainer documentation prose 'The set payload method updates specific fields while keeping others unchanged, while the overwrite method replaces the entire payload' (qdrant.tech manage-data/payload). The API's observed behavior on both faces (B: set merged; D: overwrite replaced to exactly {c}) matches both the pinned contract's actual assertion and the documented/source intent. validation_absent does not apply — the replace semantics the contract pins on the PUT face is implemented and executed correctly in the very same log.

mundane_explanation.surviving: script-oracle overreach: the B-step 'EXACT {a,b} after POST set' expectation is the script author's own construction (it requires set to erase the step-A 'orig' baseline), grounded neither in the contract (which pins exact-{c} only after PUT overwrite) nor in the documentation (set = merge) nor in the source (PayloadStorage::set -> merge). The observed POST-set merge and PUT-overwrite replace are both documented, by-design behavior; the DEFECT_FOUND verdict is a testing artifact at the script link, not a product state-logic violation.
